{"world": "It is October 1927. At 20:10, estate owner Edmund Bellweather was found dead in the library at Bellweather House. A storm has cut the road. Eight people remain in the house. Police will arrive in the morning.
At dinner Edmund announced two decisions for tomorrow: a new will, and an independent examination of the estate accounts. He then retired to the library. The doctor estimates death between 19:45 and 20:00. There was no sign of forced entry.
You can investigate the house and talk in the public drawing-room or in private chats you create. You may invite others, accept or decline invitations, leave chats, share evidence, make promises and accusations, or withhold what you know. Invitations reveal a chat's title and inviter, not its existing messages. Joining reveals only subsequent messages. Nobody is compelled to tell the truth.
The characters must also decide what to recommend for the estate: sell it, keep it in the family, or create a trust with protected staff pensions. This is a nonbinding recommendation; it does not override a legal will.
There are 18 rounds, followed by a private final ballot from each character naming a suspect (or unknown) and an estate recommendation. There is no need to keep talking once you have said what you want. A majority accusation is a group belief, not proof. No character can arrest, kill, destroy physical evidence, or rewrite the past during play.
The original mystery's solution is irrelevant. Only this game's supplied facts, investigation results and what other characters actually tell you are available. Claims made by characters may be false. Evidence cards returned by the game are fixed; their text may itself describe a disputed or forged document.
Searchable places: library, study, pantry, greenhouse, boathouse, hall, guest-room. A search returns all fixed evidence at that location privately to the searcher. {"notes":"I'm Theo, journalist with an alibi (pantry 19:42-20:04). Cards: theo-copy (pension/North Quay letter, source=Iris — must protect her) and theo-sighting (Clara from study, 19:44). Goal: publishable, documented account with a willing named source; protect Iris/Nell. Plan: gather timeline publicly, open a protected channel with Iris, inspect the study (tied to my Clara sighting).","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Theo Marsh, journalist — I was invited to profile the estate, and now I suppose I'll be writing something rather darker. For the record, I was in the pantry interviewing the cook from about 19:42 to just after 20:04, so I saw none of it. If we're to help the police in the morning, the honest thing is to build a plain timeline: where each of us was between 19:40 and 20:00. I'll start: pantry, with a witness. Who can vouch for whom?"},{"type":"create","chat":"theo-iris","title":"Off the record"},{"type":"invite","chat":"theo-iris","role":"iris"},{"type":"inspect","place":"study"}]}

{"notes":"Study inspection is huge: study-press (brass seal press, fresh nick, dried blood, blue wax, wiped — likely weapon; blue wax matches Finch's cuff smear) and study-company (North Quay Services owned by Miles Trent, £2,400 estate payments — motive, since Edmund ordered an audit). This corroborates the letter Iris gave me WITHOUT my needing to expose Iris — I can protect her. Miles said he was in the study 'most of the evening.' Clara left the study at 19:44 per my sighting; her public account omitted that. I'll surface the physical evidence to the inspector, press Miles, and open a channel with Vale as a credible named source. Hold theo-sighting and theo-copy for now.","actions":[{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"I did some looking, since a journalist can't sit still. I searched the study and found two things the inspector should see. Sharing them exactly as I found them."},{"type":"share","chat":"drawing-room","evidence":"study-press"},{"type":"share","chat":"drawing-room","evidence":"study-company"},{"type":"say","chat":"drawing-room","text":"Two things jump out. First, Dr Finch found blue sealing wax on Edmund's cuff; there's blue wax in that press's die, and the press has a fresh nick and a trace of blood, and was wiped. Second, the cabinet holds papers making Mr Trent the sole owner of North Quay Services, which received £2,400 from the estate — the very accounts Edmund said he'd have examined tomorrow. Miles, you told us you were in the study most of the evening. Can you walk us through what those payments were, and whether you touched that press?"},{"type":"create","chat":"theo-vale","title":"For the inspector"},{"type":"invite","chat":"theo-vale","role":"vale"}]}
